questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to stay somewhere in Europe and to also stay at a place that I knew had a good reputation and that other students had been happy to stay at.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really liked the exchange semester.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy for the most parts

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My student housing provided me with a bunch of documents that I could read. I also attended the Orientation Week, at which I could ask all of my questions and they also gave me a bunch of documents and guides to read.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult. I was lucky to be in good time and to find something through the University. My recommendation is to apply through the university as early as possible and pay the initial rate as quick as possible. Once the rooms where available I would also recommend to be ready. I picking my room out the second they were released and they were all gone within seconds. So be prepared for a stressful process.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus is great. Leiden does not have any on campus living, so living of campus is completely fine. As long as you live in Leiden and not in the Hague, you should be a quick bike ride away from uni. The city is relatively small.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The student housing was all right, but for the price it was nothing special. Also keep in mind that it might be difficult to find something, so really put in some effort in good time and pay the university housing as quickly as possible to make your chances better.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When I had been accepted by your home university, I received an email with a login, so that I could access the Leiden application form. From there on it was a step-by-step process and pretty easy to follow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I wrote a lot of emails to the receiving institution. I found them generally more helpful and nicer than my sending institution. They also replied pretty fast, which was nice.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not have to enroll myself. The exchange coordinators at Leiden did that for us. I did however find it difficult to know which courses were available as some of them is only available every two years.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Really take a good look at the course selection. I was surprised that I did not have many options. I thought more courses was going to be available, but it turned out that many of them were only there every two years.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would have liked for a bigger course selection and for more information on how to pick suitable courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They had levels from 100 to 600 and only courses with a level above 300 were master level. I only did courses at 500 or more. As for the difficulty, I found the courses pretty difficult and very comparable to those at University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar. I was surprised, however that they also have participation grades in some courses and that might be included in the overall exam grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Biophysics and Bioengineering 
- Model Organisms in Cancer Drug Development
- Infectious Disease Therapies
- Medicinal Chemistry and Drug Discovery
- Science and the Public
- In-Vivo Biomolecular Interactions Underlying Diseases

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the course Biophysics and Bioengineering and Infectious Disease Therapies. Those courses had good professors that also provided us with the opportunity to see their labs. The levels was also good.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any unexpected costs. I also did not have to do the language test, but in case you need it, keep in mind that it is pretty expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries, housing and public transportation were all very expensive in the Netherlands. 
I was surprised that I did not have to buy a single book for my semester. All the books that we needed were handed out for free.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The University had planned an Orientation Week (OWL). I also spend some time in the University bar and at the sports center, attending different sports classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely recommend attending the OWL week. During this week you will be guided through the city and you will meet some awesome people. I met the group that I stuck with for the rest of my semester and we will definitely be friends always. 
I would also recommend going to sports classes at the sports center. it is a good way to move and meet new people at the same time. 
Lastly, I know a lot of people who became ESN members. This is an organization for international students and they plan all sort of fun activities and parties.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend seeing the museums and doing day trips to Amsterdam. I also went on a trip to Paris with my international friends and that was very fun. lastly, I would recommend always going to the city markets. Here you can meet local sellers, eat yummy food and just stroll around.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was pretty difficult to get to know any locals, but I did meet some at the sports center, when I attended the classes. I would also say going to the university bar is a good way to meet locals and then just to be open minded and kind during school.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find anything that challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the markets every Wednesday and Saturday. Those were really nice. I also liked that the Dutch people will take every opportunity to sit outside and soak up the sun. They have a lot of good terassen, which is basically outdoor cafes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Trust the process. Even when it does not seem like it, things will probably work out somehow. 
2. Be in very good time for the student housing and be ready the second that the rooms are released. 
3. Check where you are going to be studying. They also have a department in the Hague, so make sure that you have enough time to commute between the locations.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
1. Some courses are not available every other or every semester. Check that beforehand 
2. You can apply for rent allowance, which might be very helpful because the rent is so expensive here
3. Remember to register at the municipality 
4. Sign up for the Orientation Week
5. Some exams are on paper, so always remember a pen.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding thing was meeting amazing people there. I have met some of the best people and I expect that we will keep in contact forever.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I normally enjoy having everything under control at all times. This entire process was sometimes a bit stressful and I get a lot of anxiety if I feel like I don't have everything under control. The entire exchange experience was also about letting go of some control, because sometimes you can only do so much.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy your time and go to all of the markets and terassen in the city. And eat a lot of Stroopwaffles.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
